items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: In the middle thirties in the height of the big band era, there were some really great musicians, some who came here and made a mark for themselves, Freddy Zito, Phil Olivello, a few.

ctx.x: People talk about, up there anyway, they talk about how Central New York used to be a pretty good music avenue.

Utica is remarkable. In the middle thirties in the height of the big band era, there were some really great musicians, some who came here and made a mark for themselves, Freddy Zito, Phil Olivello, a few. In the thirties in Utica my father played with Billie Holiday and Helen Humes. I know because I worked with Helen Humes later and she told me about it. “I knew your father.” I said, “Well what’d you know about him?” “Well he was good looking.” But he could play too. He never showed me a thing. I never lived with…
It’s interesting that you ended up playing the drums too.
